title: Communications and the Internet
subtitle: browse, bookmark, log in, server, wiki
summary: Talk about the Internet with confidence - browsers and search engines, logging in and subscribing, servers and attachments, blogs, wikis and online gaming.

lesson.heading: The Internet and the Web
lesson.text: The **Internet** (or **the net**) is a network connecting millions of computer users worldwide. The **World Wide Web** (or **the Web**) is a huge portion of the Internet containing linked documents, called **pages**.

examples.text: If you have a **broadband** connection, your access to the Internet should be fast.
Many cafes now offer a **wi-fi** connection, so you can get online through a **wireless** network, without a cable of any kind.

lesson.note: WWW stands for World Wide Web.

lesson.heading: Finding things online
lesson.text: When you **browse**, you look for information on the Internet. The software that helps you do this is a **browser**. You use a **search engine** to locate what you want - people now even talk about **googling** someone or something.

examples.text: Firefox is a **browser**; Google is a **search engine**.
You can easily spend a whole evening **surfing the net**.
examples.note: surfing = navigating around the Internet, sometimes aimlessly

lesson.heading: Websites
lesson.text: A **website** is a document on the Web giving information about a particular subject, person or institution. Its introductory page is the **home page**, and from there **links** take you to other pages. A good website is easy to **navigate**, i.e. to find your way around.

examples.note: FAQ stands for 'frequently asked questions' - a list of common questions with helpful answers.

examples.text: You can **bookmark** websites that you visit frequently.
If a website gets a lot of **hits**, a lot of people have visited it.

lesson.heading: Getting into a site - and out again
rows: the name you are known by on the site
the secret combination of letters and digits you type in
enter the site with your details
leave the site (the opposites of log in / log on)
a network of servers on the Internet where data can be stored and viewed from any device

lesson.heading: Online communication
lesson.text: You can communicate by **email**, and with an email you can include an **attachment** - you can **attach** a photo, for example. You can also send someone an **e-card**.

examples.text: A **server** is a powerful central computer from which other computers get information.
If your **internet service provider**'s server is **down**, you may not be able to send emails.
examples.note: down = not functioning; internet service provider is usually shortened to ISP

lesson.heading: Talking and seeing
lesson.text: You can use your computer to **Skype** friends and family - the software lets you make phone calls over the Internet and shows which people on your **contact list** are **online** at the same time. If you each have a **webcam**, you can see each other as you talk.

examples.text: I **Skype** my cousins in Australia every Sunday - I love seeing them as well as talking to them.
Is Ana **online**? Her name is on my **contact list** but it's grey.

lesson.heading: Interactive sites
lesson.text: Many online programs are **interactive**, i.e. they let users become involved in the exchange of information. **Social networking sites** are a popular way of keeping in touch with friends.

examples.text: A **wiki** is a website which allows users to add, delete and edit its contents. Wikipedia is perhaps the world's largest **wiki**.
**Blogs** are interactive too - a kind of online diary that readers can add comments to.
Many people are involved in **online gaming**, playing with people they have never met.
These games often make use of **virtual reality**.
examples.note: virtual reality = images and sounds produced by a computer that represent a place or situation the gamer can take part in

lesson.text: Log in and log on both get you into a site; the opposites are log out and log off - never 'log on' when you mean leaving.

exercises.prompt: Match each word with its definition.

pairs.right: email addresses and phone numbers for the people you know
something that you send with an email
the combination of letters and digits you use to log in
a way of accessing a favourite website quickly
software that allows you to surf the web
a large computer that holds information for smaller computers

exercises.prompt: Match each word with its definition.

pairs.right: a company that enables you to use the web
software that helps you locate the websites you need
find your way around a website
a network of servers where you can store your data online
the introductory page of a website

exercises.explanation: The Web is the huge portion of the Internet made up of linked pages.

exercises.prompt: I read that journalist's ___ every day - he's always got something interesting to say and readers often add comments.
exercises.explanation: A blog is an online diary that readers can comment on.

exercises.prompt: I couldn't ___ the Internet last night. The server must have been down.
exercises.explanation: You access the Internet; when a server is down, nothing gets through.

exercises.prompt: It's wonderful being able to ___ my cousins who live in Australia - I love seeing them as well as talking to them.
exercises.explanation: To Skype someone is to call them over the Internet, often with a webcam.

exercises.prompt: I've decided to ___ to my favourite newspaper's website. It doesn't cost much and it has lots of interesting stuff.
exercises.explanation: To subscribe to a site is to become a member of it.

exercises.prompt: I like this website because it has lots of very useful ___ to all sorts of other sites that interest me.
exercises.explanation: Links take you from one page to another.

exercises.prompt: My brother loves online gaming, particularly ___ reality games.
exercises.explanation: Virtual reality is a computer-made place the gamer can take part in.

exercises.prompt: An ___ website is one which allows users to add comments or edit its content in some way.
exercises.explanation: Interactive programs let users become involved in the exchange of information.

exercises.statement: Google is the name of a browser.
exercises.explanation: False - Google is the name of a search engine.

exercises.statement: FAQ stands for Fast Answers to Questions.
exercises.explanation: False - it stands for Frequently Asked Questions.

exercises.statement: If a cafe says that it has wi-fi access, you can get online with your laptop there.
exercises.explanation: True - wi-fi gives you a wireless connection to the Internet.

exercises.statement: A wiki is a kind of computer device.
exercises.explanation: False - it is a type of website, one that users can add to, delete from and edit.

exercises.statement: If you send someone an e-card they will receive it in the post.
exercises.explanation: False - they will get it by email.

exercises.statement: When you want to stop using the net, you log on.
exercises.explanation: False - you log off (or log out).
